    AI Overview
    Following September 2023 brain surgery to remove a tumor, Gary Woodland has battled severe PTSD, anxiety, and fear. He openly shared in March 2026 that despite returning to the PGA Tour, he struggled with mental fatigue, panic, and felt like he was "dying inside" while competing. 
    This video shows an interview where Gary Woodland shares his emotional journey:
    42s
    TenGolf
    YouTube• Mar 26, 2026
    Key details of his struggles and recovery include: 
    • PTSD Diagnosis: The tumor was on the part of his brain controlling fear and anxiety; post-surgery, he suffered from fear of dying and intense, recurring anxiety, notes this Instagram reel and Facebook post by Golf Channel.
    • Hidden Struggles: Despite returning to play in early 2024, Woodland hid the severity of his mental battle, often crying in the scoring trailer or his car, say Instagram posts and Instagram posts.
    • Impact on Competition: He experienced intense, overwhelming symptoms at the 2024 Procore Championship, including memory issues and being easily startled.
    • Recent Breakthrough: In an emotional testament to his resilience, Woodland won the 2026 Texas Children’s Houston Open, his first win since the surgery, just weeks after publicly revealing the depth of his PTSD struggle, as discussed on ESPN and BBC Sport. 
    Woodland has continued to compete to inspire others fighting similar battles.

    “I can’t waste energy anymore hiding this..." Gary Woodland is one round away from a comeback story for the ages. He has not won since his 2019 US Open win at Pebble Beach. At the Players Championship, he opened up about recent struggles with PTSD related to a 2023 brain surgery to remove a tumor that pushed on the part of the brain that controls fear and anxiety. In the interview with @RexHoggardGC, he said: “I can’t waste energy anymore hiding this, and I’m blessed with a lot of support out here on the tour. Everyone’s just been amazing. Every week I come out and everyone’s so excited and happy that I’m back. I hear that every week — it’s so nice to see you past this, it’s so nice to see you 100 percent — and I appreciate that love and support. But inside, I feel like I’m dying, and I feel like I’m living a lie.” “I hope somebody that’s struggling sees me out here still fighting and battling and trying to live my dreams.
